## Part B - Conditional Statements

#Q1
```{r}
temp <- 33

if (temp >= 32) {
  print("Hot")
} else {
  print("Not hot")
}
```

#Q2
```{r}
age <- 17

if (age < 13) {
  print("Child")
} else if (age <= 19) {
  print("Teenager")
} else {
  print("Adult")
}
```

#Q3
```{r}
marks <- c(45, 88, 73, 100, 62)
result <- ifelse(marks >= 60, "Pass", "Fail")
print(result)
```

#Q4
```{r}
x <- 10
if (x > 5) {
  print("A")
} else if (x > 8) {
  print("B")
} else {
  print("C")
}
# R checks the conditions from top to bottom and stops at the first TRUE one.
# x > 5 is TRUE, so "A" prints. x > 8 is also TRUE, but it is never checked.
```

#Q5
```r
`if` evaluates one condition (a single TRUE/FALSE) and runs a block of code. It is best for controlling program flow, such as choosing whether to run, export or stop, or for one value with several outcomes.

`ifelse()` is vectorized: it tests every element of a vector and returns a vector of the same length. It is best for creating a new column from existing data. A plain `if` on a vector errors in R 4.2 and later (older versions use only the first element), so use `ifelse()` for columns.
```

## Part C - Importing the CSV File

#Q6
```{r}
file_path <- "students_grades.csv"

if (file.exists(file_path)) {
  grades <- read.csv(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  print("File imported successfully")
} else {
  stop("students_grades.csv not found. Check your working directory with getwd().")
}
```

```{r}
head(grades)
dim(grades)
names(grades)
str(grades)
summary(grades)
colSums(is.na(grades))
```

```{r}
nrow(grades); ncol(grades)
colSums(is.na(grades))
class(grades$Section)
range(grades$Attendance)
```

1. The grades has 15 rows and 7 columns, as the registrar described.
2. The missing value is in Midterm, with one NA (Bea Navarro, StudentID 2026011).
3. Section is text, so its type is character.
4. The lowest Attendance is 70 and the highest is 100.

```{r}
stopifnot(nrow(grades) == 15,
          ncol(grades) == 7,
          sum(is.na(grades)) == 1)
```

The "stopifnot()" stops with an error if any expectation fails and is silent if all pass.

#F1
```{r}
grades$FinalGrade <- 0.30 * grades$Quiz +
                     0.30 * grades$Midterm +
                     0.40 * grades$Final
```

Arithmetic with "NA" gives "NA", so the student with the missing midterm gets "NA". This is expected.

#F2
```{r}
grades$Result <- ifelse(is.na(grades$FinalGrade), "Incomplete",
                 ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 75, "Passed", "Failed"))
```

#F3
```{r}
grades$Remarks <- ifelse(is.na(grades$FinalGrade), "Incomplete",
                  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 90, "Excellent",
                  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 85, "Very Good",
                  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 80, "Good",
                  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 75, "Fair", "Needs Improvement")))))
```

Cutoffs are tested from highest to lowest, so a score of 92 stops at "Excellent".

#F4
```{r}
grades$AttendanceFlag <- ifelse(grades$Attendance < 80, "At Risk", "OK")
```

#F5
```{r}
grades$Honors <- ifelse(!is.na(grades$FinalGrade) &
                        grades$FinalGrade >= 90 &
                        grades$Attendance >= 90, "Yes", "No")
```

#F6
```{r}
grades$Remarks_loop <- NA_character_

for (i in seq_len(nrow(grades))) {
  fg <- grades$FinalGrade[i]
  if (is.na(fg)) {
    grades$Remarks_loop[i] <- "Incomplete"
  } else if (fg >= 90) {
    grades$Remarks_loop[i] <- "Excellent"
  } else if (fg >= 85) {
    grades$Remarks_loop[i] <- "Very Good"
  } else if (fg >= 80) {
    grades$Remarks_loop[i] <- "Good"
  } else if (fg >= 75) {
    grades$Remarks_loop[i] <- "Fair"
  } else {
    grades$Remarks_loop[i] <- "Needs Improvement"
  }
}

identical(grades$Remarks, grades$Remarks_loop)
grades$Remarks_loop <- NULL
```

#F7
```{r f7, error=TRUE}
if (grades$FinalGrade >= 75) print("Passed")
```

The grades$FinalGrade >= 75 gives a vector of 15 TRUE/FALSE/NA values, but "if" needs exactly one. In R 4.2 and later this is an error ("the condition has length > 1"). In older versions it is a warning and R uses only the first element. The "NA" is a second problem: "if (NA)" errors with "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed". The loop avoids both because each pass tests one value, and "is.na()" handles the missing one first.

```{r}
table(grades$Result)
sum(grades$AttendanceFlag == "At Risk")
sum(grades$Honors == "Yes")

# Passed: 10 students (4 Failed, 1 Incomplete)
# At Risk: 4 students
# Honors candidates: 4 students
```

## Part D - Exporting Results

#Q7
```{r}
write.csv(grades, "students_grades_processed.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
at_risk <- grades[grades$AttendanceFlag == "At Risk", ]

if (nrow(at_risk) > 0) {
  write.csv(at_risk, "at_risk_students.csv", row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  print("No at-risk students.")
}
```

```{r}
honors <- grades[grades$Honors == "Yes",
                 c("StudentID", "Name", "Section", "FinalGrade", "Attendance")]

if (nrow(honors) > 0) {
  write.csv(honors, "honors_list.csv", row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  print("No honors candidates this term.")
}
```

```{r}
check_full <- read.csv("students_grades_processed.csv")
dim(check_full)
all.equal(check_full, grades)

if (file.exists("at_risk_students.csv")) {
  check_risk <- read.csv("at_risk_students.csv")
  nrow(check_risk) == nrow(at_risk)
}

if (file.exists("honors_list.csv")) {
  check_honors <- read.csv("honors_list.csv")
  nrow(check_honors) == nrow(honors)
}
```

#Q8
```r
The `write.csv()` writes missing values as the text `NA` by default (the `na = "NA"` argument), so Bea Navarro's `Midterm` and `FinalGrade` cells show `NA`. Reading the file back turns them into real `NA` values again.
```

```{r}
readLines("students_grades_processed.csv")[12]

# Without row.names = FALSE
write.csv(grades, "temp_test.csv")
head(read.csv("temp_test.csv"), 3)
file.remove("temp_test.csv")
```
```r
Without `row.names = FALSE`, R adds an extra first column holding row numbers 1 to 15. It has an empty header, which `read.csv()` reads back as `X`. It is a useless duplicate index column.
```

```{r}
grades$Scholarship <- ifelse(is.na(grades$FinalGrade), "Pending",
                      ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 95 & grades$Attendance >= 90, "Full",
                      ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 85 & grades$Attendance >= 90, "Partial",
                             "None")))
```

```{r}

```

```{r}

```

```{r}
table(grades$Scholarship)
```

#Q10
```{r}
# 1. NA >= 75 returns NA, not TRUE or FALSE, so inside if() it would cause an error
#    and inside ifelse() it would return NA. Checking is.na() first labels the
#    missing grade "Incomplete" safely.

# 2. The comparison with NA would return NA, so the missing-grade student would never
#    get "Incomplete". With ifelse() the result would be NA, and with a plain if it
#    would be an error.

# 3. ifelse() is better for creating a whole column from a vector of values.
#    if ... else is better for controlling program flow with a single TRUE/FALSE,
#    such as checking that a file exists or running different blocks of code.

# 4. Reading the exported CSV back confirms the file was written correctly (right rows,
#    columns, NA handling, and no stray index column) before it is sent to the registrar.
```
